OnCue — MuteButton
Effective October 24, 2026

Notification access
Android grants access to notifications. OnCue uses media-session information and media-notification destinations to show track titles, artists, artwork and playback progress, control playback, and reopen the playing app or browser tab. It does not save notification messages or a listening history. Live media data and destinations are kept in memory and released when sessions end or the listener disconnects.

Local settings and backup
The app stores your chosen player, last player, glass-color preference and optional browser URLs locally. Android may back up or transfer these settings according to your device settings. Artwork, media-session data and app diagnostic files are excluded from app backup. Notification access must be granted on each device.

Other apps and sharing
The player chooser reads launchable apps and browser capabilities on your device. OnCue has no Internet permission, advertising SDK, analytics SDK or developer-operated server. It does not send your media data to MuteButton. Opening a player or saved URL hands control to that app, whose privacy policy applies.

Your control
Revoke notification access in Android Settings to stop access. Clear app storage or uninstall to remove local settings; manage device backups through Android settings. You can remove saved URLs by clearing them in setup. There are no OnCue accounts.

Contact and updates
Developer: MuteButton. Policy updates and support: https://github.com/MuteButton/OnCue/issues. Issues are public: do not include private media information, saved URLs, passwords or device logs containing personal data. See the repository privacy policy for the current policy.
